summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would impose staged market share limits on supermarket groups and create a Commissioner for Food Retailing to oversee those limits and investigate trading practices.
Supermarket group limits would fall from 40 per cent in year two to 20 per cent after year five, backed by offences and divestiture directions.
It would also regulate household retail holdings under linked market share rules, with the Commissioner defining the relevant national markets and determining business shares.
changes: Failure to comply with market share requirements could attract a $50 million penalty.
Directors could face $100,000 penalties, subject to reasonable-steps and limited-tenure defences.
The Commissioner could compel information, documents and interviews for investigations.
Investigation outcomes would have to be published, including online.
Binding directions could require businesses, suppliers or intermediaries to take action or stop specified conduct.
summary.affected: Supermarket and household retail operators, related companies, directors, suppliers, intermediaries and consumers are affected.

speeches.speaker: Bob Katter
speeches.brief: Outlined a bill to create a food retailing commissioner and reduce supermarket chains to a 20 per cent maximum market share over six years, with overseas operators limited to five per cent. Argued that supermarket concentration had undermined competition, harmed farmers and retailers, and enabled large mark-ups across food and related markets.
